key_insight: Phase-sensitive chiral-interference circuits show that composite-gate robustness must be judged at the full-circuit level, not by single-gate performance alone.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware calibration and gate benchmarking, preserving relative phase is as important as high state-transfer fidelity, especially when using composite pulses for error mitigation.
method: Encode three- and four-level chiral-resolution dynamics in compact two-qubit circuits.
Implement the enantiomer-dependent sign flip via a conditional phase gate or a final rotation sign change.
Benchmark substituted single-qubit rotations against composite gates B5, SK1, BB1, H5s, and X5 under injected angle error.
evidence_signal: On IBM hardware, the circuits produced the expected enantiomer-dependent outputs with nearly 98% probability, and H5s/X5 kept high target-state populations up to about 50% relative error versus about 8% for elementary rotations.
watch_item: Variable-rotation composite sequences can distort required relative phases, so they may fail as error-correction replacements even when they are robust for isolated gates.
paper_title: Phase-Sensitive Benchmarking of Composite Quantum Gates with Chiral-Interference Circuits on Quantum Hardware
